reading.body:
CyrusOne's Aurora campus holds 114 MW of published IT capacity across three collocated facilities, representing nearly half of Illinois's disclosed data center capacity and enough for approximately 2,850 racks at AI training density.

Illinois publishes capacity figures for only six of its fifty mapped data centers, making the state's true infrastructure invisible. The Aurora campus is the largest disclosed installation in the state, yet remains modest against the largest regional clusters elsewhere. This opacity is typical: most U.S. data center capacity goes undisclosed, so public rankings of state AI infrastructure are artifacts of reporting rather than reality.

For AI scaling, 114 MW is a meaningful but not hyperscale volume. A single frontier training run can consume gigawatts across multiple sites. Whether Aurora can support AI workloads depends entirely on power availability and grid interconnection, which are not published. Tenant occupancy, actual power draw, and expansion headroom are also unknown, so this capacity figure alone cannot predict its role in AI deployment or its contribution to grid stress.
